html:
A town on the Milo River in Upper Guinea which by the 18th century was a centre of Islamic learning and of the trade in kola, gold and captives. It was built up by the Maninka Mori, a Muslim trading and clerical people led by the Kaba family.

Its traders linked the forest to the Niger markets. In the 1870s and 1880s Samori Ture fought and then ruled the area from nearby Bissandugu. The French took Kankan in 1891 and made it the end of the railway from Conakry in 1914. It is now the main city of Upper Guinea and a stronghold of Maninka political life.
